lead: An engine cylinder draws in air, squeezes it, burns fuel to add heat, and pushes the piston down. Replacing the real engine by a closed loop of ideal air gives the Otto, Diesel and Dual cycles. The difference is how heat enters: at constant volume in Otto, at constant pressure in Diesel, and partly both in Dual. That choice fixes the p-v and T-s shape and gives each cycle its air standard efficiency. Petrol and diesel engine calculations start from these three cycles.
prereq: You need Chapter 6.1 for the air standard assumptions, and Unit 2 for non-flow processes and specific heats.

sections.h3: Otto cycle: heat added at constant volume

blocks.text: State 1 is before compression, 2 after compression, 3 after heat addition, and 4 after expansion. The four processes are: 1-2 isentropic compression, 2-3 constant-volume heat addition, 3-4 isentropic expansion, and 4-1 constant-volume heat rejection. In Otto, v₂ = v₃ and v₄ = v₁. The compression ratio is r = v₁/v₂ = v₄/v₃.

For ideal air, T₂/T₁ = r^(γ−1) and T₃/T₄ = r^(γ−1). Here T is absolute temperature in kelvin, v is specific volume in m³/kg, and γ = c_p/c_v is the ratio of specific heats. Heat in q_in = c_v(T₃ − T₂). Heat out q_out = c_v(T₄ − T₁). Net work w_net = q_in − q_out.

blocks.where: η_Otto is the air standard efficiency; r is the compression ratio v₁/v₂; γ is c_p/c_v.

items: Use T₂ = T₁ r^(γ−1) and T₄ = T₃/r^(γ−1).
Factor (T₃ − T₁ r^(γ−1)) and cancel it. The result is 1/r^(γ−1).

blocks.text: On the p-v diagram, 2-3 and 4-1 are vertical constant-volume lines and 1-2 and 3-4 are isentropic curves. The Otto cycle is the air standard model of a spark-ignition petrol engine.

sections.h3: Diesel cycle: heat added at constant pressure

blocks.text: The Diesel cycle replaces the constant-volume heat addition by constant-pressure heat addition. Process 1-2 is isentropic compression, 2-3 is constant-pressure heat addition, 3-4 is isentropic expansion, and 4-1 is constant-volume heat rejection. The compression ratio is still r = v₁/v₂. The cutoff ratio is r_c = v₃/v₂ = T₃/T₂.

Heat in is at constant pressure, so q_in = c_p(T₃ − T₂); c_p is the specific heat at constant pressure. Heat out is q_out = c_v(T₄ − T₁). Net work is q_in − q_out. The expansion gives T₄ = T₁ r_c^γ. Dividing gives q_out/q_in = (r_c^γ − 1)/(γ r^(γ−1)(r_c − 1)).

blocks.where: η_Diesel is the air standard efficiency; r = v₁/v₂ is the compression ratio; r_c = v₃/v₂ is the cutoff ratio; γ = c_p/c_v.

blocks.text: On p-v, line 2-3 is now horizontal, while 4-1 remains vertical. The Diesel cycle is the air standard model of a compression-ignition engine. For the same r, Diesel efficiency is lower than Otto efficiency when r_c > 1.

sections.h3: Dual cycle: heat added in two steps

blocks.text: The Dual cycle adds heat in two steps. Process 1-2 is isentropic compression, 2-3 is constant-volume heat addition, 3-4 is constant-pressure heat addition, 4-5 is isentropic expansion, and 5-1 is constant-volume heat rejection. The compression ratio is r = v₁/v₂. The pressure ratio is r_p = p₃/p₂. The cutoff ratio is r_c = v₄/v₃ = T₄/T₃.
Heat in q_in = c_v(T₃ − T₂) + c_p(T₄ − T₃). Heat out q_out = c_v(T₅ − T₁). Net work w_net = q_in − q_out. Efficiency is 1 − q_out/q_in.

blocks.where: η_Dual is the air standard efficiency; r = v₁/v₂ is the compression ratio; r_p = p₃/p₂ is the pressure ratio; r_c = v₄/v₃ is the cutoff ratio; γ = c_p/c_v.

blocks.text: When r_p = 1, the constant-volume part vanishes and the formula becomes the Diesel formula. When r_c = 1, the constant-pressure part vanishes and the formula becomes the Otto formula. Some syllabi call this the mixed cycle or the limited pressure cycle. On p-v, 2-3 is vertical and 3-4 is horizontal.

figure.caption: The vertical lines 2-3 and 4-1 are constant volume; the curves 1-2 and 3-4 are isentropic. The pressures are p₂ = 18.4 bar, p₃ = 48.1 bar and p₄ = 2.62 bar, as in the worked example.

examples.question: An air standard Otto cycle has compression ratio 8. Air at state 1 is at 1 bar and 300 K. Heat added is 800 kJ/kg. Take c_v = 0.718 kJ/kg·K and γ = 1.4. Find T₂, T₃, T₄, the air standard efficiency, the heat rejected, the net work, p₃ and p₄.
steps: At constant volume, q_in = c_v(T₃ − T₂). T₃ = T₂ + q_in/c_v = 689.2 + 800/0.718 = 689.2 + 1114.2 = 1803.4 K.
At constant volume 4-1, p₄/p₁ = T₄/T₁. p₄ = 1 × 785.0/300 = 2.62 bar.
examples.check:
T1 = 300.0
p1 = 1.0
r = 8.0
qin = 800.0
cv = 0.718
gamma = 1.4
a = r**(gamma - 1)
T2 = T1 * a
T3 = T2 + qin / cv
T4 = T3 / a
eta = 1 - 1 / a
qout = cv * (T4 - T1)
wnet = qin - qout
p2 = p1 * r**gamma
p3 = p2 * T3 / T2
p4 = p1 * T4 / T1
print(f'{T2:.1f}')
print(f'{T3:.1f}')
print(f'{T4:.1f}')
print(f'{eta:.4f}')
print(f'{qout:.1f}')
print(f'{wnet:.1f}')
print(f'{p3:.1f}')
print(f'{p4:.2f}')

traps: Do not swap r = v₁/v₂ with r_c = v₃/v₂. r covers the whole compression stroke; r_c covers only the constant-pressure heat addition in Diesel or Dual.
Use c_p, not c_v, for the constant-pressure heat addition in Diesel and in the constant-pressure part of Dual. The examiner checks this in the first line.
Temperatures in T₂/T₁ = r^(γ−1) must be in kelvin. Putting 300°C instead of 573 K gives a wrong r^(γ−1).
In Dual, r_p = p₃/p₂, not p₃/p₁. The pressure ratio starts after compression, at state 2.
The Otto formula depends only on r and γ. The Diesel efficiency also depends on r_c; do not use 1 − 1/r^(γ−1) for a Diesel cycle.

quiz.q: List the four processes of the Otto cycle in order.
quiz.a: 1-2 isentropic compression; 2-3 constant-volume heat addition; 3-4 isentropic expansion; 4-1 constant-volume heat rejection.

quiz.q: Why does the Diesel cycle use c_p for heat addition but c_v for heat rejection?
quiz.a: Heat addition 2-3 is at constant pressure, so q = c_p ΔT. Heat rejection 4-1 is at constant volume, so q = c_v ΔT.

quiz.q: An Otto cycle has r = 6 and γ = 1.4. Find η.
Show that the Dual cycle formula becomes the Diesel formula when r_p = 1.
quiz.a: Put r_p = 1: numerator r_p r_c^γ − 1 = r_c^γ − 1; denominator (r_p − 1) + γ r_p(r_c − 1) = γ(r_c − 1). The result is 1 − (1/r^(γ−1))[(r_c^γ − 1)/(γ(r_c − 1))], the Diesel formula.

quiz.q: A Diesel cycle has r = 16, r_c = 2 and γ = 1.4. Find η.
Why can a diesel engine use a higher compression ratio than a petrol engine?
quiz.a: A diesel engine ignites fuel by compression, not by a spark. It has no fuel-air mixture in the cylinder during compression, so knock from premature spark ignition is avoided and higher r is practical.

quiz.q: In a Dual cycle, what happens to the p-v diagram when r_c = 1?
quiz.a: The constant-pressure heat addition 3-4 has zero volume change and zero heat. The cycle reduces to the Otto cycle: 1-2 compression, 2-3 constant-volume heat addition (all heat), 3-5 expansion, 5-1 rejection.

beyond: Not for the exam. Real engine models use a finite heat-release rate, wall heat transfer and variable specific heats. The Dual cycle is a bridge to those models because it separates the fast premixed burn (constant volume) from the slower diffusion burn (constant pressure). Search for 'finite heat release engine cycle' and 'Diesel engine simulation' to go further.
